Hi all — quick tax treatment summary from Sales Ops / Billing standpoint:

- For B2B SaaS (company pays, provides valid EU VAT ID) the standard approach is to issue the invoice net and include theVAT reverse-charge note ("VAT due by recipient"), assuming the supplier (Redwood) is outside the customer's VAT jurisdiction for place-of-supply rules. That lets the customer self-account.
- OSS is intended for B2C or distance sales when the seller collects VAT on supplies to consumers in multiple EU countries; it usually doesn't apply for documented B2B transactions with a validated VAT ID.
- Marketplace/platform fees can complicate things if Redwood is considered the "marketplace operator" under local rules. For now our recommendation:
  1) Split the invoice lines: subscription (seat fee) as net with reverse-charge if VAT ID validates and the buyer attests B2B usage; marketplace/platform fee — treat according to contractual terms (we can invoice it net as well if buyer is the recipient of the supply and has a VAT ID).
  2) If Procurement prefers a single invoice, we will annotate each line with tax treatment and include the VAT ID and a reverse-charge statement.

Next steps I suggest:
- We validate the VAT number (VIES) and capture the registered billing entity.
- Marissa to confirm whether Redwood Finance needs additional attestation (signed form) to apply reverse-charge.
- We'll reissue the invoice with the PO number and new remit details and mark it as "reissued — tax treatment confirmed" so your AP team sees the change.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call today if you want to walk through the PO details.
